baseline: U.S. structural and scenario parameters; none is reassigned to Portugal by this audit

Fixed.name: sigma
Fixed.mapping_note: Task substitution elasticity; cannot copy as Portuguese estimate without a model assumption/review.

Fixed.name: s_L0
Fixed.mapping_note: Labor income share; derive using comparable factor-income accounting incl. self-employed, not compensation/GDP unadjusted.

Fixed.name: cog_share
Fixed.mapping_note: Model share of AI-sensitive C employment; Eurostat ISCO occupational major groups do not directly identify the paper's C group.

Fixed.name: eps
Fixed.mapping_note: Capital-supply elasticity; open-economy Portugal/euro area capital flows may invalidate closed-country calibration.

Fixed.name: r_bar
Fixed.mapping_note: Gross no-AI rental return to capital; not a bond interest rate nor observable without income/stock conventions.

Fixed.name: delta
Fixed.mapping_note: Depreciation relative to capital stock; match asset coverage, net/gross and accounting period.

Fixed.name: lam
Fixed.mapping_note: Returns to research input: conceptual structural parameter, not a single national observation.

Fixed.name: fishing_out_R
Fixed.mapping_note: Difficulty-of-discovering-ideas parameter: non-identifiable directly from a Portuguese statistic.

Fixed.name: g
Fixed.mapping_note: No-AI idea-stock trend; observed GDP growth or labour productivity is not automatically equivalent.

Fixed.name: n
Fixed.mapping_note: Trend labor-force growth (not one year employment growth); estimate from consistent multi-year Portuguese labour-force series.

Fixed.name: iota_R0
Fixed.mapping_note: Research share of GDP in the paper's ideas block; national R&D expenditure requires a strict concept and denominator check.

Fixed.name: g_iota
Fixed.mapping_note: Growth of research share; requires consistent multi-year national research investment data and model concept crosswalk.

Fixed.name: t0
Fixed.mapping_note: Chosen comparison base year; retain 2024 until a separately reviewed redesign.

Fixed.name: t_anchor
Fixed.mapping_note: Mid-2026 scenario anchor date; not a measured Portuguese macro parameter.

Fixed.name: t_target
Fixed.mapping_note: Forecast horizon convention, not national calibration.

Fixed.name: q_bar_ann
Fixed.mapping_note: Baseline yearly quit/separation rate; E-to-U quarterly transitions alone do not capture employer-to-employer quits.

Fixed.name: q_resp_share
Fixed.mapping_note: Share of quits responding to labor-market prospects; needs econometric identification, not a public count.

Fixed.name: q_rel_C
Fixed.mapping_note: Group-C relative quit rate; requires C/N occupational mapping and longitudinal separation estimates.

Fixed.name: q_rel_N
Fixed.mapping_note: Group-N relative quit rate; requires C/N occupational mapping and longitudinal separation estimates.

Fixed.name: U_bar
Fixed.mapping_note: Baseline normal search pool. 2024 unemployment is a candidate statistic, NOT automatically equal to this model concept.

Fixed.name: mu_bar
Fixed.mapping_note: Normal-times cross-group search discount; E/U/I flows do not identify movements C↔N.

Fixed.name: iota_match
Fixed.mapping_note: Curvature of vacancy/search matching function; transfer only as sensitivity assumption or estimate from flow data.

Fixed.name: fill_bar
Fixed.mapping_note: Mean MONTHLY vacancy filling rate: requires hires and duration/stock data; vacancy rate is not a substitute.

Fixed.name: xi
Fixed.mapping_note: Downward adjustment/rigidity of AI-sensitive wage; requires worker-level or wage-series structural estimation.

Fixed.name: h
Fixed.mapping_note: Monthly numerical time-step retained; not nationally re-estimated.

Fixed.name: cc_rates
Fixed.mapping_note: Continuously compounded rate-conversion switch, keep as computational convention.

Scenario.name: m_anchor
Scenario.mapping_note: Mid-2026 task mass reachable by AI; firm AI use and occupation exposure are not equivalent task mass.

Scenario.name: m_2030
Scenario.mapping_note: Future technical task reach in 2030; scenario assumption, not observation.

Scenario.name: d_anchor
Scenario.mapping_note: Task-level AI diffusion mid-2026, not percentage of firms using any AI.

Scenario.name: d_2030
Scenario.mapping_note: Future task-level adoption, requires assumptions about intensity and occupational mix.

Scenario.name: a_anchor
Scenario.mapping_note: Log gain in task-level productivity, not observed wage or GDP growth.

Scenario.name: g_a
Scenario.mapping_note: Annual slope in assumed task-level productivity gains; not a country measured growth rate.

Scenario.name: d_ceiling
Scenario.mapping_note: Logistic adoption ceiling set by model, not a measured penetration statistic.

Scenario.name: psi
Scenario.mapping_note: Labor substitution fraction among AI activity; not AI enterprise use rate.

Scenario.name: rho
Scenario.mapping_note: Number of newly reinstated human tasks per automated task; empirical target currently unavailable.

Scenario.name: mu
Scenario.mapping_note: Scenario labor-search discount; do not confuse with normal-times mu_bar or a published occupational transition probability.

Scenario.name: theta_H
Scenario.mapping_note: Firm posting speed per month; quarterly vacancy stock does not identify it.

INE_EMPLOYMENT_2024.organization: Portugal DGE reporting INE Employment Statistics
INE_EMPLOYMENT_2024.description: Annual mean unemployment rate, employed and unemployed persons

INE_EMPLOYMENT_2025.organization: Portugal DGE reporting INE Employment Statistics

AMECO_WAGE_SHARE.description: Adjusted wage share, ensure same valuation and self-employment treatment as model labor share; national value not retrieved

AMECO_CAPITAL.description: Capital stocks, depreciation and income accounts; no direct capital-supply elasticity

EUROSTAT_ISCO.description: Employment by ISCO-08 occupation; requires explicitly documented C/N classification crosswalk

EUROSTAT_LFS_FLOWS.description: Observed E/U/I transitions, not C-to-N occupational transitions, employer quits, or monthly vacancy fill rates

EUROSTAT_MICRODATA.description: Restricted anonymized EU-LFS microdata for qualified scientific research, may help occupational crosswalk and transitions

EUROSTAT_VACANCIES.description: Vacancy STOCK and rates, not vacancy FILL rate

INE_ENTERPRISE_AI_2025.description: 11.5 percent of businesses using AI is NOT the share of tasks performed with AI

US_REPRODUCTION.organization: Fernando Hoces de la Guardia independent reimplementation
US_REPRODUCTION.description: Exact immutable U.S. model reference and parameter types

PT_RND_GERD_2024.organization: PORDATA compiling Eurostat and INE R&D data
PT_RND_GERD_2024.description: 2024 gross domestic R&D expenditure about 1.72% of GDP (marked provisional). A distinct proxy, not directly the model's ideas-sector iota_R0.

verified_context_observations.label: Annual average unemployment rate
verified_context_observations.note: Candidate normal-times unemployment calibration; requires age/definition alignment and matching to steady-state search pool.

verified_context_observations.label: Annual average employed persons
verified_context_observations.note: Context statistic; not a direct model parameter because model labor force is normalized.

verified_context_observations.label: Annual average unemployed persons
verified_context_observations.note: Context statistic; distinguish ILO unemployed from all job seekers.

verified_context_observations.label: Annual average unemployment rate, context only
verified_context_observations.note: Not a substitute for 2024 base-year calibration.

verified_context_observations.label: Enterprises reporting any AI use, 2025
verified_context_observations.note: 2025 business adoption among covered enterprises, not labor/task-level diffusion m or d.

verified_context_observations.label: Gross domestic expenditure on R&D / GDP (provisional)
verified_context_observations.note: GERD is total domestic research expenditure, not necessarily the model's ideas-input share; conceptual mapping and years must be checked before use.

calibration_gates: Create a source-verified, occupational ISCO→paper C/N crosswalk and quantify classification uncertainty.
Align 2024 labor share (national accounts), unemployment pool and 2024 labor force into consistent model definitions.
Estimate baseline job finding, separations, vacancy fill and between-group mobility; do not substitute Eurostat E/U/I flows for C↔N.
Review small-open-economy capital-supply closure, investment inflows and migration; keep U.S. structural elasticities labeled as assumptions.
Keep all seven AI scenario dials as explicit alternative assumptions; national firm-level AI adoption is contextual only.
Require all parameter values with provenance, units, dates, transformations and uncertainty ranges before enabling country simulation.
Run U.S. original tests unchanged and independent Portugal-specific base-year and time-series validation prior to any PT 2030 headline.
